ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p341/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p341/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p341/r4.claim: Earlier nations rejected warnings of the Hereafter and sound prophetic arguments, treating a human prophet as an insult; God destroyed them in this world and will punish them in the next.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p341/r4.anchor: nations which denied the warnings of their respective prophets about the Hereafter and vainly rejected their sound arguments

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p347/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p347/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p347/r1.claim: Past nations rejected messengers despite clear signs, arrogantly objecting that ordinary human beings could not be divinely appointed guides.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p347/r1.anchor: these nations denied them because of arrogance and haughtiness and made up false excuses such as: asking why the Almighty made human beings His messengers

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p347/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p347/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p347/r2.claim: By these objections the nations rejected their messengers and their call to truth, so God left them to face the consequences.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p347/r2.anchor: by making such objections and excuses, these people rejected their messenger and his calls to the truth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p347/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p347/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p347/r3.claim: God arranges guidance for people's benefit, but does not force it on those who fail to value it; He is self-sufficient.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p347/r3.anchor: if the Almighty wants to guide people it is not because this is something which is to His benefit

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p189/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p189/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p189/r4.claim: Earlier unbelievers, like Quraysh, incredulously asked whether human beings could guide them, reasoning that all humans were equal and asking how messengers could be distinguished.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p189/r4.anchor: كما استبعدت قريش، فقالوا على سبيل الاستغراب: أبشر يهدوننا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p189/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p189/r5.speaker: الحوفي وابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p189/r5.claim: Al-Ḥawfī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya parse “human beings” as the subject and “guide us” as its predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p189/r5.anchor: وارتفع أبشر عند الحوفي وابن عطية على الابتداء، والخبر يهدوننا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p189/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p189/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p189/r6.claim: He prefers parsing “human beings” as the agent of the verb, since the interrogative hamza seeks a verb; he treats the construction as اشتغال.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p189/r6.anchor: والأحسن أن يكون مرفوعا على الفاعلية، لأن همزة الاستفهام تطلب الفعل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p189/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p189/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p189/r7.claim: The ف in “so they disbelieved” marks disbelief immediately following the messengers' clear proofs: they failed to consider the proofs and instead rejected them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p189/r7.anchor: العطف بالفاء يدل على تعقب كفرهم مجيء الرسل بالبينات،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p189/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p189/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p189/r8.claim: استغنى means simply that God showed his self-sufficiency by destroying them; his self-sufficiency is eternal, so the form does not mean seeking sufficiency.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p189/r8.anchor: استغنى الله: استفعل بمعنى الفعل المجرد، وغناه تعالى أزلي،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p189/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p189/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p189/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says God's independence appeared because he did not compel them to believe despite having power to do so; Abū Ḥayyān calls this a Muʿtazilī insinuation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p189/r9.anchor: حيث لم يلجئهم إلى الإيمان، ولم يضطرهم إليه مع قدرته على ذلك.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p141#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p141#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p141#2/r2.claim: In ‘human messengers guide us,’ البشر is grammatically singular but collective in meaning, with إنسان as its individual; they object that a human like them guides them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p141#2/r2.anchor: لأن البشر وإن كان لفظه واحدا فإنه في معنى الجمع، وهو اسم الجنس لا واحد له من لفظه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p141#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p141#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p141#2/r3.claim: God has no need of their faith and is independent of creation, praiseworthy in His acts.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p141#2/r3.anchor: عن إيمانهم {والله غني} عن خلقه {حميد} في أفعاله.

JISHUMI:v10p6955/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6955/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6955/r1.claim: In bi-annahu, the hāʾ may be an expletive support or a pronoun referring to firmness.
JISHUMI:v10p6955/r1.anchor: قيل: الهاء عماد، وقيل: كناية عن الثبات

JISHUMI:v10p6955/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6955/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6955/r2.claim: The punishment came because messengers brought clear proofs, arguments, and miracles, but people denied them and turned away; God needs neither them nor their worship and only commands for their benefit.
JISHUMI:v10p6955/r2.anchor: ذلك العذاب نزل بهم لأجل أن الرسل أتتهم بالبينات والحجج والمعجزات فأنكروا

JISHUMI:v10p6955/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6955/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6955/r3.claim: God is described as self-sufficient and praiseworthy: either praised, or deserving praise for blessing people despite their disbelief.
JISHUMI:v10p6955/r3.anchor: والله غني لا تجوز عليه الحاجة حميد قيل: محمود، وقيل: من حقه أن يحمد لإنعامه عليهم مع كفرهم

JISHUMI:v10p6956/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6956/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6956/r1.claim: The phrase that punishment came because of their deeds shows that punishment is deserved for sins, which are their own acts.
JISHUMI:v10p6956/r1.anchor: أن العقاب يستحق على المعاصي، وأن المعاصي فعلهم

JISHUMI:v10p6956/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p6956/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p6956/r2.claim: By asking whether ordinary humans could guide them, the people showed their inability to answer the manifest miracle and shifted to an irrelevant objection; prophethood concerns benefit, not shared species.
JISHUMI:v10p6956/r2.anchor: عجزوا عند ظهور المعجزة، فعدلوا إلى ما ليس بحجة؛ لأن الرسالة لا تتعلق بالجنس

ELMALILI:64:1-10#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:64:1-10#3/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:64:1-10#3/r8.claim: The painful worldly punishments of Noah's, ʿĀd's, Thamūd's, Lot's, and Pharaoh's peoples warn present unbelievers; a more painful punishment awaits them in the Hereafter.
ELMALILI:64:1-10#3/r8.anchor: Nûh kavmi, Âd ve Semûd ve kavm-i Lût ve Firavun gibi küfürde ısrar edenlerin küfürlerinin

ELMALILI:64:1-10#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:64:1-10#3/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:64:1-10#3/r9.claim: Earlier peoples were punished because messengers brought clear proofs but they objected that humans could not guide them, disbelieved, and turned away.
ELMALILI:64:1-10#3/r9.anchor: onlara peygamberleri beyyinelerle, açık deliller, mucizelerle geliyorlardı da bunlara karşı o kâfirler

ELMALILI:64:1-10#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:64:1-10#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:64:1-10#3/r10.claim: God showed that He had no need of their faith or obedience by destroying them; He is self-sufficient from all creation and worthy of praise.
ELMALILI:64:1-10#3/r10.anchor: gösterdi onların ne iman ve tâatlerine ne de kendilerine asla ihtiyâcı bulunmadığını anlattı

ELMALILI:64:1-10#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:64:1-10#3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:64:1-10#3/r11.claim: Ghanī means God is independent of the entire universe and can replace it; Ḥamīd means He possesses every perfection and deserves praise.
ELMALILI:64:1-10#3/r11.anchor: Allah Ganî’dir sade onlardan değil, bütün âlemînden ganîdir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r7.speaker: İnkârcılar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r7.claim: Their common argument against accepting prophets is summarized as: a human being cannot guide us.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r7.anchor: “Bir beşer mi bizi doğru yola çıkaracak!” şeklinde özetlenmiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r8.speaker: Zemahşerî ve Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r8.claim: The phrase that God showed Himself unneedful can mean He does not need their faith and worship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r8.anchor: Onların imanına ve kulluğuna muhtaç olmadı, muhtaç olmadığını gösterdi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r9.speaker: Zemahşerî ve Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r9.claim: It can also mean God did not compel them to believe despite having power to do so.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r9.anchor: Gücü yettiği halde onları imana zorlamadı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r10.speaker: Zemahşerî ve Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r10.claim: Another explanation is that God demonstrated perfection by presenting clear proof without coercing them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:64:6/r10.anchor: Ortaya koyduğu açık ve kesin kanıtlarla yetinmek ve onları zorlamamak suretiyle kemalini gösterdi

RAZI-FULL:v30p21#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p21#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p21#2/r2.claim: “That is because” means the matter was that they objected to a human messenger guiding them; they did not object to worshipping stone idols, so they disbelieved and turned away.

RAZI-FULL:v30p21#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p21#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p21#2/r3.claim: God had been independent of their obedience and worship from pre-eternity.
RAZI-FULL:v30p21#2/r3.anchor: واستغنى الله عن طاعتهم وعبادتهم من الأزل

RAZI-FULL:v30p21#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p21#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p21#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥamīd means either the one inherently deserving praise or the one who praises.
RAZI-FULL:v30p21#2/r4.anchor: والحميد بمعنى المحمود أي المستحق للحمد بذاته ويكون بمعنى الحامد

RAZI-FULL:v30p21#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p21#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p21#2/r13.claim: “They turned away” is not redundant with “they disbelieved”: their rejection of human messengers expressed complete refusal and turning away, hence both verbs.
RAZI-FULL:v30p21#2/r13.anchor: وهذا في معنى الإنكار والإعراض بالكلية

RAZI-FULL:v30p21#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p21#2/r14.speaker: الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v30p21#2/r14.claim: The Kashshāf explains the sequence as God’s independence becoming manifest when He did not compel them to faith, despite having power to do so.

STUDYQURAN:64:6/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:64:6/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:64:6/r1.claim: Incredulity that God would send human messengers is a recurring barrier to belief, documented at 17:94 and many other verses.
STUDYQURAN:64:6/r1.anchor: one of the constant barriers to belief, as in 17:94

STUDYQURAN:64:6/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:64:6/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:64:6/r2.claim: The same human-messenger objection was made against Muhammad's prophethood, as in 25:7.
STUDYQURAN:64:6/r2.anchor: This same objection is attributed to those who rejected the prophethood of Muhammad

STUDYQURAN:64:6/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:64:6/r3.speaker: R, Z
STUDYQURAN:64:6/r3.claim: God's Self-Sufficiency may mean He has no need of people or their belief and, though able, did not compel them to believe.
STUDYQURAN:64:6/r3.anchor: could indicate that God has no need of them or no need for them to believe in Him; thus He did not compel them to believe in Him despite His ability to do so (R, Z)

STUDYQURAN:64:6/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:64:6/r4.speaker: Āl
STUDYQURAN:64:6/r4.claim: God's being Praised is intrinsic to the Divine Nature and does not depend on anyone praising Him; the epithet often accompanies Self-Sufficiency, as in 4:131, 14:8, 22:64, 31:12, 31:26, 35:15, and 60:6.
STUDYQURAN:64:6/r4.anchor: being praised is intrinsic to the Divine Nature and not dependent upon anything to praise Him (Āl)

TAB-FULL:v23p8/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p8/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p8/r1.claim: Addressing Quraysh’s polytheists, al-Ṭabarī recalls earlier disbelieving peoples, including Noah’s, ʿĀd, Thamūd, Abraham’s, and Lot’s communities.
TAB-FULL:v23p8/r1.anchor: كفروا من قبلكم، وذلك كقوم نوح وعاد وثمود وقوم إبراهيم وقوم لوط.

TAB-FULL:v23p8#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p8#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p8#2/r1.claim: Earlier peoples were punished because messengers brought clear proofs establishing their call’s truth, but the people arrogantly rejected human messengers and the truth brought by their peers.
TAB-FULL:v23p8#2/r1.anchor: والإعلام على حقيقة ما يدعونهم إليه، فقالوا لهم: أبشر يهدوننا؟

TAB-FULL:v23p8#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p8#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p8#2/r2.claim: Their question rejects the idea that human beings like themselves could guide them, expressing disdain for following truth from their own kind.
TAB-FULL:v23p8#2/r2.anchor: فقالوا لهم: أبشر يهدوننا؟ استكبارا منهم أن تكون رسل الله إليهم بشرا مثلهم

TAB-FULL:v23p8#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p8#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p8#2/r3.claim: The verb is plural because bashar, singular in form, carries a collective meaning; hence “they guide us,” not “he guides us.”
TAB-FULL:v23p8#2/r3.anchor: وجمع الخبر عن البشر، فقيل: يهدوننا، ولم يقل: يهدينا، لأن البشر، وإن كان في لفظ الواحد

TAB-FULL:v23p8#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p8#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p8#3/r1.claim: They disbelieved and turned away from truth; God needed none of them, for He is independent of all creation.
TAB-FULL:v23p8#3/r1.anchor: منهم حاجة. {والله غني حميد} [التغابن: 6] يقول: والله غني عن جميع خلقه

TAB-FULL:v23p8#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p8#3/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p8#3/r2.claim: God has no need of them or their faith in Him and His messengers, and needs nothing from them.
TAB-FULL:v23p8#3/r2.anchor: منهم حاجة. {والله غني حميد} [التغابن: 6] يقول: والله غني عن جميع خلقه

TAB-FULL:v23p8#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p8#3/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p8#3/r3.claim: God is independent of all creation and praised by all for His favors and generous acts toward them.
TAB-FULL:v23p8#3/r3.anchor: يقول: والله غني عن جميع خلقه، محمود عند جميعهم بجميل أياديه عندهم، وكريم فعاله فيهم.

BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r2.claim: The unbelievers’ worldly suffering did not expiate their sins, since they still face punishment; sound reports say worldly pains and misfortunes expiate believers’ sins.
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r2.anchor: وفيه أخبار بأن ما أصابهم في الدنيا لم يكن كفارة لذنوبهم وإلا لم يعذبوا في الآخرة

BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r3.claim: ذلك refers to both the punishment they tasted in worldly life and the punishment they will taste in the hereafter.
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r3.anchor: أي ما ذكر من العذاب الذي زاقوه في الدنيا وما سيذوقونه في الآخرة

BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r4.claim: The cause was that messengers came to them with clear signs and miracles.
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r4.anchor: أي بالمعجزات الظاهرة والباء إما للملابسة أو للتعدية

BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r5.claim: The preposition باء in بالبينات may indicate accompaniment or make the phrase transitive.

BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r7.claim: أبشر means ‘human beings,’ as the Persian gloss also renders it as human beings like us.
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r7.anchor: أي قال كل قوم من المذكورين في حق رسولهم الذي أتاهم بالمعجزات منكرين لكون الرسول من جنس البشر

BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r8.claim: Each people expressed astonishment that a human like themselves could guide and direct them in religion, toward God, or toward closeness to Him.
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r8.anchor: متعجبين من ذلك ابشر وآدمى مثلنا يهدينا ويرشدنا إلى الدين أو إلى الله والتقرب منه

BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r9.claim: The author compares their objection with Thamud’s question about following two humans from among themselves.
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r9.anchor: كما قالت ثمود ابشرا منا واحدا نتبعه أنكروا أن يكون الرسول بشرا

BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r10.claim: The account generalizes the saying across communities, assigning each people’s objection to its own messenger; بشر is a generic noun expressed with a plural description.
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r10.anchor: فأسند القول إلى جميع الأقوام وأريد البشر الجنس

BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r11.claim: أبشر is preferably the subject of an omitted verb explained by يهدوننا, an instance of الاشتغال; this is better than a nominal sentence because an interrogative calls for an explicit or implicit verb.
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r11.anchor: وارتفاع بشر على أنه فاعل فعل مضمر يفسره ما بعده فيكون من باب الاشتغال وهو أولى من جعله مبتدأ

BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r12.speaker: القاشاني
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r12.claim: Al-Qashani says ego-centered traits kept them from the light by which a messenger surpasses others immeasurably; seeing only his humanity, they denied his guidance.
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r12.anchor: لما حبوا بصفات نفوسهم عن النور الذي هو به يفضل لعيهم بما لا يقاس ولم يجدوا منه إلا البشرية أنكروا هدايته

BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r13.speaker: القاشاني
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r13.claim: Al-Qashani explains that recognition requires a corresponding meaning within the knower: innate light recognizes perfection, and only the perfect knows perfection; no one knows God but God.
BURSEVI:v10p5#2/r13.anchor: فإن كان كل عارف لا يعرف نمعروفه إلا بالمعنى الذي فيه فلا يوجد النور الكمالي

BURSEVI:v10p6/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p6/r1.speaker: القاشاني
BURSEVI:v10p6/r1.claim: Al-Qashani continues that a person who believes something must find some of its meaning within, or they could not turn toward it; thus people without innate light could not recognize the messengers’ perfection or seek guidance.
BURSEVI:v10p6/r1.anchor: وكذا كل مصدق بشيء فإنه واجد للمعنى المصدق به بما في نفسه من ذلك المعنى

BURSEVI:v10p6/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p6/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p6/r2.claim: Lacking any innate light, they failed to recognize the messengers’ perfection or the truth and never developed a need for guidance, so they denied guidance itself.
BURSEVI:v10p6/r2.anchor: فلما لم يكن فيهم شيء من النور الفطري

BURSEVI:v10p6/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p6/r3.speaker: بعض العارفين
BURSEVI:v10p6/r3.claim: Some gnostics say recognizing a perfected saint is harder than knowing God: God is known by perfection and majesty, whereas a saint visibly shares ordinary human weakness and bodily needs.
BURSEVI:v10p6/r3.anchor: معرفة مقام الأولياء أصعب من الممكن من معرفة الله تعالى لأن الله تعالى معروف بكماله وجماله

BURSEVI:v10p6/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p6/r4.speaker: بعض العارفين
BURSEVI:v10p6/r4.claim: They add that if the saint’s reality were unveiled people would worship him as they worshipped Jesus, and his inner radiance would eclipse the sun and moon.
BURSEVI:v10p6/r4.anchor: والله لو كشف للخلق عن حقيقة الولي لعبد كما عبد عيسى عليه السلام ولو كشف لهم عن مشرقات نوره

BURSEVI:v10p6/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p6/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p6/r5.claim: God veils saints’ rank as mercy: it keeps people from knowingly warring against God when they harm a saint and gives ignorant offenders an excuse, since people have harmed saints in every age.
BURSEVI:v10p6/r5.anchor: ولكن في ستر الحق تعالى لمقام الولي حكم وأسرار وأدنى ما في الستر أن لاي تعرض أحد لمحاربة الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v10p6/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p6/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p6/r6.claim: They disbelieved because the objection belittled the messengers and they failed to understand the wisdom in choosing human messengers.
BURSEVI:v10p6/r6.anchor: أي بالرسل بسبب هذا القول لأنهم قالوه استصغارا لهم ولم يعلموا الحكمة في اختيار كون الرسل بشرا

BURSEVI:v10p6/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p6/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p6/r7.claim: They turned away from considering the evidence brought by the messengers and from believing them.
BURSEVI:v10p6/r7.anchor: عن التدبير فيما أتوا به من البينات وعن الإيمان بهم

BURSEVI:v10p6/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p6/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p6/r8.claim: God showed that He needed neither their belief nor obedience by destroying them and cutting off their line; if He needed either, He would not have done so.
BURSEVI:v10p6/r8.anchor: أي أظهر استغناءه عن إيمانهم وطاعتهم حيث أهلكهم وقطع دابرهم ولولا غناه تعالى عنهما لما فعل ذلك

BURSEVI:v10p6/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p6/r9.speaker: سعدي المفتي
BURSEVI:v10p6/r9.claim: Sa‘di al-Mufti parses استغنى as a circumstantial clause with an understood قد, from the triliteral verb, and says it conveys complete independence because seeking entails need.
BURSEVI:v10p6/r9.anchor: وقال سعدي المفتي هو حال بتقدير قد وهو بمعنى ني الثلاثي والمراد كمال الغني إذ الطلب يلزمه الكمال

BURSEVI:v10p6/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p6/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p6/r10.claim: God is independent of all creation, and therefore especially independent of their belief and obedience.
BURSEVI:v10p6/r10.anchor: عن العالمين فضلا عن إيمانهم وطاعته

BURSEVI:v10p6/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p6/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p6/r11.claim: Every creature praises God by its state and thereby indicates His perfection, whether or not His enemies praise Him.
BURSEVI:v10p6/r11.anchor: يحمده كل مخلوق بلسان الحال ويدل على اتصافه بالصفات الكمالية لأ يحمده أولياؤه وإن امتنع أعداؤه

BURSEVI:v10p6/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p6/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p6/r12.claim: Praise is naming attributes of perfection insofar as they are perfection; recognizing God as praiseworthy in essence, attributes, and acts occupies the servant with remembrance and praise.
BURSEVI:v10p6/r12.anchor: والحمد هو ذكر أوصاف الكمال من حيث هو كمال ومن عرف إنه الحميد في ذاته وصفاته وأفعاله شغله ذكره والثناء عليه

BURSEVI:v10p6/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p6/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p6/r13.claim: However many praiseworthy beliefs, character traits, deeds, and words a human has, some fault remains by comparison with the Prophet, Muhammad, Ahmad, and Mahmoud, who is perfect in every respect.
BURSEVI:v10p6/r13.anchor: فإنه العبد وإن كثرت محامده من عقائده وأخلاقه وأفعاله وأقواله فلا يخلو عن مذمة ونقص إلى النبي عليه السلام فإنه محمد وأحمد ومحمود من كل وجه

BURSEVI:v10p6/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p6/r14.speaker: السهروردي
BURSEVI:v10p6/r14.claim: Al-Suhrawardi says regular recitation of the devotional divine name يا حميد الفعال ذا المن على جميع خلقه بلطفه brings wealth beyond counting.
BURSEVI:v10p6/r14.anchor: قال السهرورودي رحمه الله من داومه يحل له من الأموال ما لا يمكن ضبطه

TABATABAI:64:5-6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:5-6/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:64:5-6/r2.claim: God's names and attributes entail resurrection and judgment, which require revealed law; messengers convey it with warning and glad tidings. The passage moves from past disbelievers to rejection of revelation, then denial of resurrection, before faith and final reward or punishment.
TABATABAI:64:5-6/r2.anchor: لما كان مقتضى أسمائه الحسنى وصفاته العليا المعدودة في الآيات السابقة وجوب معاد الناس

TABATABAI:64:5-6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:5-6/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:64:5-6/r5.claim: The next verse identifies rejection of the messengers as the cause of both the worldly annihilation and the afterlife punishment just mentioned.
TABATABAI:64:5-6/r5.anchor: بيان لسبب ما ذكر من تعذيبهم بعذاب الاستئصال وعذاب الآخرة

TABATABAI:64:5-6/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:5-6/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:64:5-6/r6.claim: The independent clause begins without a coordinating conjunction, answering an implied question about why they suffered; ذلك points to the punishments just described.
TABATABAI:64:5-6/r6.anchor: ولذلك جيء بالفصل دون العطف كأنه جواب لسؤال مقدر

TABATABAI:64:5-6/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:5-6/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:64:5-6/r7.claim: The imperfect with كانت portrays messengers' repeated arrival, while the contrasted wording presents their rejection as one decisive, stubborn refusal.
TABATABAI:64:5-6/r7.anchor: وفي التعبير عن إتيان الرسل ودعوتهم

TABATABAI:64:6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:64:6/r1.claim: The pattern matches earlier communities who would not believe what they had already rejected; God seals the hearts of disbelievers and transgressors.
TABATABAI:64:6/r1.anchor: تلك القرى نقص عليك من أنبائها ولقد جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات

TABATABAI:64:6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:6/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:64:6/r2.claim: Bashar can be singular or plural; here it is plural, as shown by the following plural verb يهدوننا.
TABATABAI:64:6/r2.anchor: يطلق البشر على الواحد والجمع والمراد به الثاني

TABATABAI:64:6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:64:6/r3.claim: The indefinite بشر belittles the messengers, while the question rejects the idea that mere humans with no superiority over them could guide them; this reflects arrogance.
TABATABAI:64:6/r3.anchor: والاستفهام للإنكار أي قالوا على سبيل الإنكار

TABATABAI:64:6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:64:6/r4.claim: Their contemptuous objection led them to base disbelief and turning away on that claim.

TABATABAI:64:6-7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r1.claim: For God, who is rich in Himself, istighna means manifesting self-sufficiency rather than acquiring wealth.
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r1.anchor: الاستغناء طلب الغنى وهو من الله سبحانه

TABATABAI:64:6-7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r2.claim: One explanation is that people imagined their knowledge, strength, and ability guaranteed their survival; their extermination manifested God's independence from their existence.
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r2.anchor: وذلك أنهم كانوا يرون أن لهم من العلم والقوة والاستطاعة ما يدفع عن جمعهم الفناء

TABATABAI:64:6-7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r3.claim: More broadly, people presume God owes them happiness and favor; worldly consequences and afterlife punishment together show His independence from them.
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r3.anchor: فالمراد باستغنائه تعالى عنهم مجموع ما أفيد بقوله { فذاقوا وبال أمرهم ولهم عذاب أليم }

TABATABAI:64:6-7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r4.claim: Tabataba'i offers two related readings and judges the second broader; either way, the word conveys God's majesty and power.
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r4.anchor: فهذان وجهان في معنى قوله تعالى { واستغنى الله }

TABATABAI:64:6-7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r5.claim: The destruction exemplifies successive missions that nations rejected, leaving them as tales of the past.
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r5.anchor: ثم أرسلنا رسلنا تترا كلما جاء أمة رسولها كذبوه

TABATABAI:64:6-7/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r6.claim: One alternative says God needed no further guidance after establishing proof and completing the argument.
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r6.anchor: وقيل المراد واستغنى الله بإقامة البرهان وإتمام الحجة عليهم

TABATABAI:64:6-7/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r7.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r7.claim: Another alternative says God has always been independent of their obedience and worship.
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r7.anchor: وقيل المراد واستغنى الله عن طاعتهم وعبادتهم أزلا وأبدا

TABATABAI:64:6-7/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r8.claim: Tabataba'i dismisses the proof-sufficiency and worship-independence alternatives.
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r8.anchor: والوجهان كما ترى. وقوله { والله غني حميد }

TABATABAI:64:6-7/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r9.claim: The closing clause explains the judgment: God is intrinsically rich and praiseworthy in His acts; just punishment returns people's own deeds to them.
TABATABAI:64:6-7/r9.anchor: في محل التعليل لمضمون الآية، والمعنى والله غني في ذاته

TABRISI:64:6-8/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:64:6-8/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:64:6-8/r4.claim: In dhālika bi-annahu, the pronoun is the pronoun of the matter or affair.

TABRISI:64:6-8/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:64:6-8/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:64:6-8/r5.claim: Abashar is an indefinite subject licensed by the question; interrogative and negative clauses allow such subjects because they are non-assertive.
TABRISI:64:6-8/r5.anchor: أبشر مبتدأ وإنما جاز أن يكون مبتدأ مع كونه نكرة لأن الاستفهام سوغ ذلك

TABRISI:64:6-8/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:64:6-8/r6.speaker: قول آخر
TABRISI:64:6-8/r6.claim: Alternatively, abashar is the subject of an omitted verb explained by yahdūnanā; the verb is elided because a verb-first question is more natural.
TABRISI:64:6-8/r6.anchor: وقيل: إنه فاعل فعل مضمر يفسره قوله يهدوننا كأنه قال أيهدينا بشر

TABRISI:64:6-8/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:64:6-8/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:64:6-8/r10.claim: The nations were destroyed after messengers brought clear proofs and people rejected them as mere humans, out of contempt for following a human messenger and pride in ancestral religion.
TABRISI:64:6-8/r10.anchor: والمعنى أخلق مثلنا يهدوننا إلى الحق ويدعوننا إلى غير دين آبائنا استصغارا منهم للبشر

TABRISI:64:6-8/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:64:6-8/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:64:6-8/r11.claim: They disbelieved in God, denied His messengers, and turned away from accepting them and reflecting on their signs.
TABRISI:64:6-8/r11.anchor: { فكفروا } بالله وجحدوا رسله { وتولوا } أي أعرضوا عن القبول منهم والتفكر

TABRISI:64:6-8/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:64:6-8/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:64:6-8/r12.claim: God needs no obedience from His servants; He obligated them for their own benefit, not from need for their worship.
TABRISI:64:6-8/r12.anchor: بسلطانه عن طاعة عباده وإنما كلفهم لنفعهم لا لحاجة منه إلى عبادتهم

TABRISI:64:6-8/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:64:6-8/r13.speaker: قول آخر
TABRISI:64:6-8/r13.claim: Another explanation is that the proof and clarification God showed them made any further call to guidance unnecessary.
TABRISI:64:6-8/r13.anchor: وقيل: معناه واستغنى الله بما أظهره لهم من البرهان وأوضحه من البيان

TABRISI:64:6-8/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:64:6-8/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:64:6-8/r14.claim: God is independent of people's deeds and worthy of their praise for His blessings; alternatively, He is praised in all His acts because they are wholly beneficent.
TABRISI:64:6-8/r14.anchor: أي غني عن أعمالكم مستحمد إليكم بما ينعم به عليكم. وقيل حميد أي محمود

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p485#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p485#3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p485#3/r1.claim: God has no need of their faith or worship.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:64:5-6/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:64:5-6/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:64:5-6/r2.claim: Their punishment came because messengers brought clear proofs and they rejected them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:64:5-6/r2.anchor: ذلك } أي: ذلك الذي نزل بهم { بأنه كانت تأتيهم رسلهم بالبينات فقالوا: أبشر يهدوننا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:64:5-6/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:64:5-6/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:64:5-6/r3.claim: They considered it implausible that human beings could guide them; “human” is collective, explaining the plural “guide us.”
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:64:5-6/r3.anchor: استبعدوا أن يكون الداعي إلى الحق بشرا، والمراد بالبشر ههنا الجمع، لذلك قال: { يهدوننا،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:64:5-6/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:64:5-6/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:64:5-6/r4.claim: They disbelieved and turned away from faith.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:64:5-6/r4.anchor: فكفروا وتولوا } عن الإيمان { واستغنى الله } أي: عن إيمانهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:64:5-6/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:64:5-6/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:64:5-6/r5.claim: God has no need of their faith or of His creatures and is praiseworthy in His actions.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:64:5-6/r5.anchor: أي: عن إيمانهم { والله غني } عن خلقه { حميد } في أفعاله.

QASHANI:64:6/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:64:6/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:64:6/r1.claim: Veiled by ego, they saw only the messengers' humanity and rejected their guidance; one recognizes a reality only through a corresponding meaning within, and perfection through innate light and the perfect.
QASHANI:64:6/r1.anchor: لما حجبوا بصفات نفوسهم عن النور الذي هو به يفضل عليهم بما لا يقاس

QASHANI:64:6/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:64:6/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:64:6/r2.claim: Every seeker or believer possesses inwardly some aspect of what is sought or affirmed; lacking any innate light, these people could not recognize the messenger's perfection or the truth and thus rejected guidance.
QASHANI:64:6/r2.anchor: فلما لم يكن فيهم شيء من النور الفطري أصلا لم يعرفوا منه الكمال

QASHANI:64:6/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:64:6/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:64:6/r3.claim: They disbelieved by being veiled from truth, religion, and messenger, turning from intelligible realities toward what they could perceive with the senses.
QASHANI:64:6/r3.anchor: أي: حجبوا عن الحق والدين والرسول وأعرضوا بالتوجه إلى ما وجدوا من المحسوسات

QASHANI:64:6/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:64:6/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:64:6/r4.claim: God is self-sufficient through His perfection, possessing and witnessing His Essence whether people know Him or not.
QASHANI:64:6/r4.anchor: بكماله لأنه واجد كماله مشاهد لذاته عرفوا أو لم يعرفوا

QASHANI:64:6/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:64:6/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:64:6/r5.claim: God is self-sufficient in His Essence; no aspect of His perfection depends on human belief or knowledge.
QASHANI:64:6/r5.anchor: بذاته عن إيمانهم لا يتوقف كمال من كمالاته عليهم ولا على معرفتهم له

QASHANI:64:6/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:64:6/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:64:6/r6.claim: God is complete in Himself, with perfections manifested in all beings, especially His friends; even unseen and unpraised, each existent praises Him through its particular perfection.
QASHANI:64:6/r6.anchor: كامل في نفسه بكمالاته الظاهرة في مظاهر ذرات الوجود خصوصا على أوليائه

QUSHAYRI:v3p325/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p325/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p325/r1.claim: They viewed guidance only from the human, created side and fell into confusion; seeing through reality would free them from false multiplicity and changing conditions by witnessing God's decree.
QUSHAYRI:v3p325/r1.anchor: شاهدوا الأمر من حيث الخلق فتطوحوا في متاهات الإشكال المختلفة الأحوال . ولو نظروا بعين الحقيقة

BURHAN:v1p308/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p308/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p308/r1.claim: أبشرا is accusative in the first verse through الاشتغال because the resumed object is accusative; أبشر is nominative in 64:6 because the resumptive subject is nominative.
BURHAN:v1p308/r1.anchor: والجواب أن نصب بشرا على الاشتغال والشاغل للعامل منصوب فصح لعامله أن يفسر ناصبا وأما فى الثانية فالشاغل مرفوع مفسر رافعا

AKHFASH:v2p543#2/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p543#2/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p543#2/r1.claim: The plural verb yahdūnanā agrees with bashar because the word has a collective sense.

NAHHAS:v4p441/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p441/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p441/r14.claim: The pronoun hāʾ refers to the account, and what follows explains it as the predicate of anna.
NAHHAS:v4p441/r14.anchor: الهاء كناية عن الحديث وما بعده مفسر له خبر عن أن

NAHHAS:v4p441/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p441/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p441/r15.claim: Their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs and arguments.
NAHHAS:v4p441/r15.anchor: ( كانت تأتيهم رسلهم بالبينات ) أي بالحجج والبراهين

NAHHAS:v4p441/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p441/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p441/r16.claim: Yahdūnanā follows the plural sense of bashar, while yahdīnā would follow its singular form.
NAHHAS:v4p441/r16.anchor: فقال يهدوننا ولفظ بشر واحد تكلم النحويون في نظير هذا فقال بعضهم يهدوننا على المعنى ويهدينا على اللفظ

NAHHAS:v4p441/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p441/r17.speaker: المازني
NAHHAS:v4p441/r17.claim: Al-Mazini says three nafar or raht is allowed because these denote a small group, while qawm and bashar span larger or all numbers and do not work in that construction.
NAHHAS:v4p441/r17.anchor: وقال المازني وذكر عللا في مسائل في النحو منها أن النحويين أجازوا أن يقال جاءني ثلاثة نفر وثلاثة رهط

NAHHAS:v4p441/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p441/r18.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v4p441/r18.claim: Muhammad ibn Yazid disagrees with al-Mazini's explanation for bashar, noting that bashar can be singular or plural, as in 12:31, while agreeing on the other cases.
NAHHAS:v4p441/r18.anchor: قال بشر يكون للواحد والجميع قال الله جل وعز

NAHHAS:v4p441/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p441/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p441/r19.claim: They denied God's prophets and signs, turned away from faith, and God has no need of their belief or any creature; He is praised for His favors.
NAHHAS:v4p441/r19.anchor: أي جحدوا أنبياء الله جل وعز وآياته

SAMIN-DURR:64:6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:64:6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:64:6/r1.claim: The ه in بأنه is a pronoun of شأن and حديث; كانت تأتيهم رسلهم is its predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:64:6/r1.anchor: الهاء للشأن والحديث، و { كانت تأتيهم رسلهم } خبرها

SAMIN-DURR:64:6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:64:6/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:64:6/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says استغنى means God became manifestly self-sufficient; its initial س is not a request marker.
SAMIN-DURR:64:6/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " ظهر غناه فالسين ليست للطلب ".

SAMIN-DURR:64:6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:64:6/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:64:6/r3.claim: أبشر may be subject in اشتغال, preferred because the interrogative seeks a verb; alternatively it may be subject and predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:64:6/r3.anchor: يجوز أن يرتفع على الفاعلية، ويكون من الاشتغال، وهو الأرجح لأن الأداة تطلب الفعل

SAMIN-DURR:64:6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:64:6/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:64:6/r4.claim: The plural pronoun in يهدوننا agrees with بشر, a collective noun.
SAMIN-DURR:64:6/r4.anchor: وجمع الضمير في " يهدوننا " إذ البشر اسم جنس.

ASAD-NOTES:64:5#n5/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:64:5#n5/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:64:5#n5/r1.claim: The apostles came from among their own people, carrying divine messages specifically intended for them.
ASAD-NOTES:64:5#n5/r1.anchor: apostles from their own midst, entrusted with divine messages specifically meant for them

ASAD-NOTES:64:5#n5/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:64:5#n5/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:64:5#n5/r2.claim: The phrase behind 'time and again' implies repeated visits over a duration.
ASAD-NOTES:64:5#n5/r2.anchor: The expression "time and again" is conditioned by the phrase kanat ta'atihim which implies repetition and duration

ASAD-NOTES:64:5#n6/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:64:5#n6/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:64:5#n6/r1.claim: The rejecters' reply literally means 'guide us.'
ASAD-NOTES:64:5#n6/r1.anchor: Lit., "guide us". This negative response is characteristic of people

ASAD-NOTES:64:5#n6/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:64:5#n6/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:64:5#n6/r2.claim: Estrangement from moral standards makes people deeply distrust human beings, so they cannot accept that divine guidance may come through ordinary people lacking supernatural qualities.
ASAD-NOTES:64:5#n6/r2.anchor: their own estrangement from all moral standards, are instinctively, and deeply, distrustful of all things human

QIRAAT-ER:64:6:6#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:64:6:6#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:64:6:6#1/r1.claim: Sukūn on sīn lightens the broken plural by reducing its medial vowel.
QIRAAT-ER:64:6:6#1/r1.anchor: Sukūn on sīn — lightened pronunciation of the broken plural, reducing the medial vowel

ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r1.claim: The worldly punishment they tasted and the punishment awaiting them in the Hereafter resulted from the messengers’ coming with clear signs.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r1.anchor: ما ذكر من الذعاب الذي ذاقوه في الدنيا وما سيذوقونه في الآخرة

ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r2.claim: Each unbelieving people objected either that their messenger was a human being like them or that human beings could guide them, as Thamud asked in 54:24.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r2.anchor: منكرين لكون الرسول من جنس البشر أو مجتمعين من ذلك يهدينا كما قالت ثمود : ( أبشرا منا واحدا نتبعه )

ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r3.claim: The account generalizes the statement to all peoples, uses بشر as a collective singular with a plural predicate, and similarly generalizes the address in 23:51.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r3.anchor: وقد أجمل في الحكاية فأسند القول إلى جميع الأقوام

ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r4.speaker: الحوفي وابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r4.claim: Al-Hawfi and Ibn Atiyya parse بشر as a nominative subject, with يهدوننا as its predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r4.anchor: وجملة ( يهدوننا ) هو الخبر عند الحوفي وابن عطية

ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r5.claim: Al-Alusi prefers parsing بشر as the subject of an omitted verb explained by يهدوننا, since the interrogative hamza favors a verb and the construction is from باب الاشتغال.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r5.anchor: والأحسن أن يكون مرفوعا على الفاعلية بفعل محذوف يفسره المذكور لأن همزة الأستفهام أميل إلى الفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r6.claim: They disbelieved in the messengers and turned away from reflecting on the signs and believing in them.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r6.anchor: على التأمل فيما أتوا من البينات وعن الإيمان بهم

ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r7.claim: God displayed His independence of their faith and obedience by destroying them and ending their line; the alternative circumstantial parsing is less apt than coordination.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r7.anchor: أظهر سبحانه غناه عن إيمانهم وعن طاعتهم حيث أهلكهم وقطع دابرهم ولو لا غناه عز وجل عنهما لما فعل ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r8.claim: An alternative parses واستغنى الله as a circumstantial clause after their disbelief and turning away; al-Alusi prefers treating it as coordinated with what precedes.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r8.anchor: والجملة عطف على ما قبلها وقيل : في موضع الحال على أن المعنى ( فكفروا وتولوا ) وقد استغنى الله تعالى عن كل شيء والأول هو الوجه

ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r9.claim: God is praised by every creature through the eloquence of its state, or He is inherently worthy of praise even if no one praises Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v28p122#2/r9.anchor: يحمده كل مخلوق بلسان الحال الذي هو أفصح من لسان المقال أو مستحق جل شأنه للحمد بذاته وإن لم يحمده سبحانه حامد

BAYDAWI-FULL:64:4-6/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:64:4-6/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:64:4-6/r7.claim: Dhālika refers to the previously mentioned worldly consequence and punishment.

BAYDAWI-FULL:64:4-6/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:64:4-6/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:64:4-6/r8.claim: The messengers brought miracles; people objected in surprise that human beings should guide them, though bashar can refer to one person or a group.
BAYDAWI-FULL:64:4-6/r8.anchor: أنكروا وتعجبوا من أن يكون الرسل بشرا

BAYDAWI-FULL:64:4-6/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:64:4-6/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:64:4-6/r9.claim: Bashar is used for either an individual or a group.

BAYDAWI-FULL:64:4-6/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:64:4-6/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:64:4-6/r10.claim: They disbelieved in the messengers and turned away from reflecting on the clear signs.

BAYDAWI-FULL:64:4-6/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:64:4-6/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:64:4-6/r11.claim: God is independent of everything, especially their obedience and worship.
BAYDAWI-FULL:64:4-6/r11.anchor: عن كل شيء فضلا عن طاعتهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:64:4-6/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:64:4-6/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:64:4-6/r12.claim: God needs no worship, and every creature displays His praiseworthiness.

SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.claim: A fronted or postponed locative does not raise the noun: the noun remains a nominative subject, while the locative supplies its setting, as in fīhā ʿAbd Allāh.
SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.anchor: فعبد الله ارتفع بالابتداء لأن الذي

SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.claim: A locative before the subject can form a complete sentence, and an inna construction allows it to be shifted after the noun without changing its role.
SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.anchor: ألا ترى أنك لو قلت فيها عبد الله حسن السكوت وكان كلاما مستقيما

SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.claim: When the locative precedes a nominative predicate it may be ungoverning; with an accusative predicate it separates subject from predicate, and the subject licenses the circumstantial accusative.
SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.anchor: قد حالت بين المبتدإ والقائم واستغنى بها فعمل المبتدأ حين لم يكن القائم

SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.claim: A locative can mark where a state holds while the predicate remains built on its subject, as in huwa laka khāliṣ or ʿAbd Allāh qāʾim fīhā.
SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.anchor: ومن قال فيها عبد الله قائم قال هو لك خالص

SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.claim: The phrase khāliṣa yawma l-qiyāma is read with khāliṣa nominative or accusative; the accusative is more common because it functions like a verbal noun, khulūṣan.
SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.anchor: وقد قرى هذا الحرف على وجهين @QB@ قل هي للذين آمنوا في الحياة الدنيا

SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.claim: Predicates can precede a locative and be accusative as circumstantial modifiers; rajul ṣidq maʿlūman describes a fact in that state, while nominative can make the word adjectival.
SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.anchor: في الشعر قد انتصب خبره وهو مقدم قبل الظرف قوله

SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.claim: Khalīl analyzes ḥasana ummuhu karīman abūhā as describing a quality established for the mother in that circumstance; nominative is also possible as an adjective.
SIBAWAYH:لأنهخبرلمعروفيرتفععلىالابتداءقد.anchor: مررت برجل حسنة أمه كريما أبوها زعم الخليل أنه أخبر

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: Afaʿala commonly makes an intransitive verb causative: dakhala, kharaja, and jalasa become adkhalahu, akhrajahu, and ajlasahu when another agent causes the action.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: تقول دخل وخرج وجلس فإذا أخبرت أن غيره صيره إلى شيء من هذا قلت أخرجه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: Faʿala and afaʿala can sometimes share causative meaning, as in fariḥa/farriḥahu or afraḥahu, gharima/gharramahu or aghramahu, and similar pairs.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: وقد يجيء الشيء على فعلت فيشرك أفعلت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: The forms ṭaradtu and aṭradtu differ: the first means I drove him away, while the second means I made him a fugitive; hounds ṭaradna the game by driving it along.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: وأما طردته فنحيته وأطردته جعلته طريدا هاربا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: Ṭalaʿa means appeared, aṭlaʿa ʿalayhim means came upon them, šariqa means appeared, and ašraqa means shone; asraʿa means hastened and abṭaʾa means delayed.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: ويقال طلعت أي بدوت وطلعت الشمس أي بدت وأطلعت عليهم أي هجمت عليهم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: Saraʿa and baṭuʾa describe inherent qualities like lightness and heaviness and are not transitive, unlike ṭawwaltu l-amr or ʿajjalته.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: غريزة كقولك خف وثقل ولا تعديهما إلى شيء كما تقول طولت الأمر وعجلته

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: Khalīl says fatanahu and ḥazanahu mean putting temptation or grief into someone, like kaḥaltuhu and dahantuhu; making someone tempting or sad instead takes aftanahu or aḥzanahu.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: فتنته وحزنته لم ترد أن تقول جعلته

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: Shatara r-rajulu and shatarat ʿaynuhu are distinct formations; to make a man squint, use aštarahu, just as afzaʿahu differs from faziʿa.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: وشترت عينه فإذا أردت تغير شتر الرجل لم تقل إلا أشترته

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: بعضهم
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: One group transmits Nuṣayb's poetic line with sawadtu, as in sawadtu fa-lam amlik sawādī.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: وقد اختلفوا في هذا البيت لنصيب ~~فقال بعضهم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: بعضهم
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: Another group reads the line as suddat, interpreting it as a faʿalt form.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: وقال بعضهم ~~سدت يعني فعلت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: بعض العرب
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: Some Arabs use aftantu, aḥzantu, arjaʿtu, and aʿwartu ʿaynahu to mean making someone or something acquire that state.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: وقال بعض العرب أفتنت الرجل وأحزنته وأرجعته وأعورت عينه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: Several verbs allow paired intransitive and transitive forms for putting a state into something, including jabara/jabartuhu and rakaḍat/rakaḍtu.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: جبرت يده وجبرتها وركضت الدابة وركضتها

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: The faʿalt causative meaning to make someone become something is rare; examples are faṭartuhu fa-afṭara and bashartuhu fa-abshara.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: وقد جاء فعلته إذا أردت أن تجعله مفعلا وذلك فطرته فأفطر

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: Khaṭṭaʾtuhu means called him a wrongdoer, like calling someone fāsiq or zānī; ḥayyaytuhu is a greeting, while saqaytuhu and raʿaytuhu can express a prayer for him.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: فأما خطأته فإنما أردت سميته مخطئا كما أنك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: العرب
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: Asqaytuhu is also used in the sense of saqaytuhu; Dhū al-Rumma's poem about watering the ruins illustrates this usage.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: معنى سقيته فدخلت على فعلت كما تدخل فعلت عليها

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: Afaʿaltuhu can expose someone to an event, as in aqtaltuhu, exposed him to killing; qabartuhu means buried him, while aqbartuhu provided him a grave.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: على أن تعرضه لأمر وذلك قولك أقتلته أي عرضته للقتل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: Saqaytuhu means he drank what I gave; asqaytuhu means I provided water and a supply, paralleling kasawtuhu/albastuhu; shafaytuhu cures, while ashfaytuhu gives a cure.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: جعلت له ماء وسقيا ألا ترى أنك تقول أسقيته أي جعلت له ماء وسقيا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: Afaʿala can mean acquiring a condition: ajraba, anḥaza, and aḥāla mean becoming affected by mange, wasting, or livestock loss; related forms describe a person who owns such traits or resources.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: وتقول أجرب الرجل وأنحز وأحال

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: Alāma r-rajulu means he became deserving of blame, whereas lāmahu means he reproached him; similar forms describe having abundant or scarce means.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: ومثل ذلك قول الرجل ألام الرجل أي صار صاحب لائمة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: Aṣrama, amḍagha, aḥṣada, and ajazza describe crops that have become ready to be cut, chewed, or harvested; the simple verb reports actually doing the act.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: ومثل هذا أصرم النخل وأمضغ وأحصد الزرع وأجز النخل وأقطع

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: Ḥamidtu means I rewarded him and gave his due, whereas aḥmadtu means I found him deserving of praise, like crops becoming ready for cutting.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: وقالوا حمدته أي جزيته وقضيته حقه فأما

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: Arāba means becoming a person of suspicion, while rābanī means causing suspicion in me; the distinction parallels becoming worthy of blame versus reproaching someone.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: وقالوا أراب كما قالوا ألام أي صار صاحب ريبة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: Khalīl says some faʿalt/afʿalt pairs have the same meaning but differ by dialect, such as qalaltu/alqaltu, šaġaltu/ašġaltu, and bakartu/abkartu.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: زعم ذلك الخليل فيجيء به قوم على فعلت ويلحق قوم فيه الألف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: Sībawayh gives further synonymous dialect forms, including qalaltu/alqaltu, šaġaltu/ašġaltu, ṣarra/aṣarra, and bakara/abkara.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: قلته البيع وأقلته وشغله وأشغله وصر أذنيه وأصر أذنيه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: Aṣbaḥnā, amsaynā, asḥarnā, and afjarnā mean entering those times of day; ṣabbaḥnā and similar simple forms mean visiting someone then.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: في حين صبح ومساء وسحر

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: Verbs such as yušajjaʿu, yujabbanu, and yuqawwā describe someone being labeled or charged with those qualities; šanuʿa can similarly be said of a person.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: وما بني على يفعل يشجع ويجبن ويقوى أي يرمي بذلك ومثله قد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: Ghallaqa can describe repeated work closing many doors; aghlaqa is also good for plural doors, and al-Farazdaq's verse attests aghliqu abwāban.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: وقالوا أغلقت الباب وغلقت الأبواب حين

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: أبو عمرو
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: Abū ʿAmr distinguished nazaltu from anzaltu.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: وكان أبو عمرو أيضا يفرق بين نزلت وأنزلت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.claim: Abāna and istabāna can be used with or without the added object form to mean that a thing became clear or that one made it clear, with paired forms sharing meaning.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابافتراقفعلتوأفعلتفيالفعلل.anchor: ويقال أبان الشيء نفسه وأبنته واستبان واستبنته والمعنى واحد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفعلمنهعلىغيرفعلته)#.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفعلمنهعلىغيرفعلته)#.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفعلمنهعلىغيرفعلته)#.claim: Forms such as majnūn, maslūl, and mazqūm derive from underlying verbs like janantuhu or salaltuhu even when those verbs are unused; replacement verbs can make the unused forms unnecessary.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفعلمنهعلىغيرفعلته)#.anchor: وإنما جاءت هذه الحروف على جننته وسللته وإن لم يستعمل في الكلام

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفعلمنهعلىغيرفعلته)#.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفعلمنهعلىغيرفعلته)#.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفعلمنهعلىغيرفعلته)#.claim: Janna and salla can mean putting madness or illness into someone, like ḥazuna and raḏula; janantuhu means I put madness in you, parallel to aqbartuhu giving someone a grave.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفعلمنهعلىغيرفعلته)#.anchor: جعل فيه الجنون والسل كما قالوا حزن وفسل ورذل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r1.claim: The passage explains earlier nations’ destruction and deliverance as God's act, then identifies the rejection of messengers as the cause.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r1.anchor: ولما ذكر ما أحله بهم سبحانه وأشار إلى القطع بأنه من عنده

BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r2.claim: “That” refers to the great calamity, which decisively shows that disbelief is utterly false and angers the Creator.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r2.anchor: أي الأمر الشنيع العظيم من الوبال الدال قطعا على أن الكفر أبطل الباطل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r3.claim: Unlike Ghāfir, this sūra does not aim to classify people into two groups; classification appears incidentally to establish the Hour, so the pronoun of the matter is enough.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r3.anchor: ولما لم يكن مقصودها كمقصود غافر من تصنيف الناس صنفين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r4.claim: The messengers came to their own peoples habitually, chosen by God to bring them clear proofs, including scriptures that unmistakably establish their mission and make the punishment more severe.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r4.anchor: أي رسل الله الذين أرسلهم إليهم وخصهم بهم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r5.claim: Human dignity is rightly asserted against rebellious devils but wrongly becomes pride against God’s friends; the disbelievers misplaced their self-regard.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r5.anchor: فمن وضعها موضعها بالتكبر على من أمر الله بالتكبر عليه وهم شياطين الإنس والجن ممن عصاه سبحانه نجا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r6.claim: Bashar is a generic human category and is nominative as the agent because the interrogative calls for a verb.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r6.anchor: أي هذا الجنس وهو مرفوع على الفاعلية لأن الاستفهام

BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r7.claim: The plural verb preserves the collective force of the messengers’ rejection; a singular would lose the awe of their combined denial.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r7.anchor: وكان لو أفرد الضمير لم يكن له روعة الجمع

BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r8.claim: They disbelieved immediately and without reflection, out of envy that human messengers equal them in humanity and received a special commission.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r8.anchor: بذلك عقب مجيء الرسل وبسببه من غير نظر وتفكر وأدنى تأمل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r9.claim: They reasoned that God’s greatness required nonhuman messengers, but reflection would show that ordinary people could not bear seeing angels; prophets receive added capacity, and humans are more receptive to their own kind.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r9.anchor: وهم الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام بقوى زائدة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r10.claim: Messengers serve creatures’ interests, not God’s; when people turn away, God leaves them to their choice, harming only themselves.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r10.anchor: ولما كان هذا كله إنما هو لمصالح الخلق لا يعود على الله سبحانه وتعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r11.claim: God has always been independent of all creation and eternally possesses complete perfection and praise; nothing newly accrues to Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p9/r11.anchor: له صفة الغنى المطلق والحمد الأبلغ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r2.claim: The demonstrative advances an indirect allusion toward near-explicit warning: earlier people’s matching words brought punishment, so those who speak like them may suffer the same.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r2.anchor: كانت مقالة الذين من قبل مماثلة لمقالة المخاطبين فإذا كانت هي سبب ما ذاقوه من الوبال فيوشك أن يذوق مماثلوهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r3.claim: The demonstrative refers back to the previously mentioned calamity and painful punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r3.anchor: فاسم الإشارة عائد إلى المذكور من الوبال والعذاب الأليم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r4.claim: This counts another form of their unbelief: rejecting the Messenger and the Quran, which is itself a clear proof because it is a miracle.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r4.anchor: فهذا عد لكفر آخر من وجوه كفرهم وهو تكذيبهم الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم وتكذيبهم بالقرآن فإن القرآن بينة من البينات لأنه معجزة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r5.claim: The causal باء makes the clause a reason, while the pronoun is ضمير الشأن, magnifying the explanatory clause about messengers bringing proofs and the people’s reaction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r5.anchor: والباء للسببية فالجملة في موقع العلة . والضمير ضمير الشأن لقصد تهويل ما يفسر الضمير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r6.claim: Their rejecting question assumes humans cannot guide humans; this ignorance of human capacities and God’s choice of messengers made them refuse the Quran, though only a messenger of their own kind could guide them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r6.anchor: والاستفهام في { أبشر } استفهام إنكار وإبطال فهم أحالوا أن يكون بشر مثلهم يهدون بشرا أمثالهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r7.claim: بشر is a generic noun for a human, usable for one person or a group, as shown by its use of the Prophet and in the story of Joseph and Mary.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r7.anchor: والبشر : اسم جنس للإنسان يصدق على الواحد كما في قوله تعالى : { قل إنما أنا بشر مثلكم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r8.claim: بشر is indefinite to indicate a kind, since the object of denial is human nature in those who guide them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r8.anchor: وتنكير بشر } للنوعية لأن محط الإنكار على كونهم يهدونهم ، هو نوع البشرية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r9.claim: Fronting the subject before the verbal predicate strengthens their denial; because they truly believed human messengers impossible, they judged the messengers false and consequently disbelieved.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p268/r9.anchor: وتقديم المسند إليه على الخبر الفعلي لقصد تقوي حكم الإنكار ، وما قالوا ذلك حتى اعتقدوه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p269/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p269/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p269/r1.claim: Tawallī literally means leaving one’s place and is used metaphorically here for turning away from accepting the messengers’ call.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p269/r1.anchor: والتولي أصله : الانصراف عن المكان الذي أنت فيه ، وهو هنا مستعار للإعراض عن قبول دعوة رسلهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p269/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p269/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p269/r2.claim: استغنى is Form X, with س and ت intensifying the sense; it means God is independent of their faith.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p269/r2.anchor: واستغنى } غني فالسين والتاء للمبالغة كقوله : { أما من استغنى } ( عبس : 5 ) . والمعنى : غني الله عن إيمانهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p269/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p269/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p269/r3.claim: The waw can be circumstantial: God had been independent of their faith from eternity, since His independence is eternally established.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p269/r3.anchor: والواو واو الحال ، أي والحال أن الله غني عنهم من زمن مضى فإن غنى الله عن إيمانهم مقرر في الأزل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p269/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p269/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p269/r4.claim: Alternatively, God dispensed with renewing their summons because the proofs were sufficient for belief absent obstinacy, and therefore hastened their punishment; on either reading the omitted object is their faith.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p269/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد : واستغنى الله عن إعادة دعوتهم لأن فيما أظهر لهم من البينات على أيدي رسلهم ما هو كاف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p269/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p269/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p269/r5.claim: The closing clause generalizes that God needs nothing they are asked to do and is praiseworthy by those who obey and give thanks.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v28p269/r5.anchor: وجملة { والله غني حميد } تذييل ، أي غني عن كل شيء فيما طلب منهم ، حميد لمن امتثل وشكر .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p318#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p318#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p318#2/r4.claim: Earlier unbelievers' objection resembles Quraysh's rejection of human resurrection and prophethood, compounded by envy of the chosen messenger.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p318#2/r4.anchor: ثم ذكر تعالى من مقالة أولئك الماضين ما هو مشبه لقول كفار قريش من استبعاد بعث الله للبشر، ونبوة أحد من بني آدم، وحسد الشخص المبعوث

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p318#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p318#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p318#2/r5.claim: أبشر is nominative as the sentence's subject.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p318#2/r5.anchor: وقوله: أبشر رفع بالابتداء، وجمع الضمير في قوله: يهدوننا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p318#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p318#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p318#2/r6.claim: The plural in يهدوننا reflects that بشر names the human species: they ask whether people are to guide them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p318#2/r6.anchor: وجمع الضمير في قوله: يهدوننا من حيث كان البشر اسم هذا النوع الآدمي، كأنهم قالوا أناس هداتنا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p318#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p318#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p318#2/r7.claim: Their destruction became manifest, showing they could not harm God; He was eternally self-sufficient.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p318#2/r7.anchor: وقوله تعالى: استغنى الله عبارة عما ظهر من هلاكهم، وأنهم لن يضروا الله شيئا، فبان أنه كان غنيا أزلا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p318#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p318#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p318#2/r8.claim: Although استفعل usually indicates seeking or attaining through seeking, this wording fits because God's self-sufficiency became manifest after their destruction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p318#2/r8.anchor: وبسبب ظهور هلاكهم بعد أن لم يكن ظاهرا ساغ استعمال هذا البناء مسندا إلى اسم الله تعالى، لأن بناء استفعل إنما هو لطلب الشيء وتحصيله بالطلب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p281#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p281#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p281#4/r1.claim: Their punishment came because their messengers brought clear signs and they denied them, asking whether people like themselves could guide them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p281#4/r1.anchor: ذلك الذي اصباهم بأنه كانت تأتيهم رسلهم بالبينات فينكرون ذلك ويقولون أبشر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p281#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p281#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p281#4/r2.claim: Bashar is a collective noun meaning people, although its grammatical form is singular.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p281#4/r2.anchor: والبشر اسم جنس معناه الجمع وإن كان لفظه واحد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p281#4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p281#4/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p281#4/r3.claim: They disbelieved and turned away, that is, they turned away from faith.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p281#4/r3.anchor: فكفروا وتولوا أي أعرضوا عن الإيمان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p281#4/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p281#4/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p281#4/r4.claim: God had no need of their faith or worship.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p136/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p136/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p136/r4.claim: The messengers came with clear proofs, evidences, and demonstrations.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p136/r4.anchor: ذلك بأنه كانت تأتيهم رسلهم بالبينات} أي: بالحجج والدلائل والبراهين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p136/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p136/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p136/r5.claim: They thought it implausible that messengership would belong to human beings and that a person like them could guide them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p136/r5.anchor: أي: استبعدوا أن تكون الرسالة في البشر، وأن يكون هداهم على يدي بشر مثلهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p136/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p136/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p136/r6.claim: They denied the truth and turned away from acting upon it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p136/r6.anchor: أي: كذبوا بالحق ونكلوا عن العمل،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p136/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p136/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p136/r7.claim: God had no need of them; He is self-sufficient and praiseworthy.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r1.claim: The rejecters said this to belittle human beings as messengers from God to people like themselves.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r1.anchor: يعني أن الكفار قالوا ذلك استصغارا للبشر أن يكونوا رسلا من الله إلى أمثالهم ,

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r2.claim: Bashar and insan mean the same thing, though their names have different derivations.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r2.anchor: والبشر والإنسان واحد في المعنى , وإنما يختلفان في اشتقاق الاسم ,

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r3.claim: Bashar derives from the visible surface of the skin.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r4.claim: Insan may derive from uns, human sociability.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r4.anchor: وفي الإنسان وجهان : أحدهما : مأخوذ من الإنس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r5.claim: Alternatively, insan may derive from forgetfulness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r5.anchor: أحدهما : مأخوذ من الإنس . والثاني : من النسيان .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r6.claim: They disbelieved in the messengers and turned away from the proof.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r6.anchor: فكفروا } يعني بالرسل { وتولوا } يعني عن البرهان .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r7.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r7.claim: God needs no obedience from His servants by virtue of His sovereign power.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r7.anchor: أحدهما : بسلطانه عن طاعة عباده , قاله مقاتل .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r8.claim: Alternatively, God had no need of further proof after making the signs and explanation clear enough to guide people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r8.anchor: الثاني : واستغنى الله بما أظهره لهم من البرهان وأوضحه لهم من البيان من زيادة تدعو إلى الرشد وتقود إلى الهداية .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r9.speaker: البراء بن عازب
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r9.claim: God is independent of your charitable gifts.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r9.anchor: أحدهما : غني عن صدقاتكم , قاله البراء بن عازب .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r10.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r10.claim: God is independent of your deeds.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r11.speaker: علي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r11.claim: God is worthy of praise from His creatures for the blessings He gives them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r11.anchor: أحدهما : يعني مستحمدا إلى خلقه بما ينعم به عليهم , وهو معنى قول علي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r12.claim: Alternatively, God is inherently deserving of their praise.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas gives a third explanation: God loves His servants to praise Him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p21/r13.anchor: وحكي عن ابن عباس فيه ثالث : معناه يحب من عباده أن يحمدوه .

MUQATIL:64:5-6/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:64:5-6/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:64:5-6/r2.claim: Their messengers brought clear explanations, but the people objected that humans would guide them and so disbelieved and turned away.
MUQATIL:64:5-6/r2.anchor: { كانت تأتيهم رسلهم بالبينات } يعني البيان

MUQATIL:64:5-6/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:64:5-6/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:64:5-6/r3.claim: God has no need of His creatures' worship and is rich beyond them.

MUQATIL:64:5-6/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:64:5-6/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:64:5-6/r4.claim: God is praised in His dominion by His creatures.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p251#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p251#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p251#4/r1.claim: “That” refers to the worldly punishment they tasted and the afterlife punishment prepared for them.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p251#4/r1.anchor: اشارة إلى ما ذكر من الوبال الذي ذاقوه في الدنيا وما أعدلهم من العذاب في الآخر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p251#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p251#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p251#4/r2.claim: The messengers came with clear proofs, meaning miracles.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p251#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p251#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p251#4/r3.claim: They rejected the idea that human beings could be messengers, although they did not reject worshipping stones.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p251#4/r3.anchor: أنكروا الرسالة للبشر ولم ينكروا العبادة للحجر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p251#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p251#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p251#4/r4.claim: They disbelieved the messengers and turned from faith; God has no need of creation or their faith and obedience, and is praiseworthy in His work.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p251#4/r4.anchor: اطلق ليتناول كل شيء ومن حملته ايمانهم وطاعتهم

QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r1.claim: That punishment is for disbelieving the messengers who came to them.
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { ذلك } أي هذا العذاب لهم بكفرهم بالرسل تأتيهم { بالبينات }

QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r3.claim: The rejecters object that their guides are human beings, denying that a messenger could be human.
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r3.anchor: أنكروا أن يكون الرسول من البشر

QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r4.claim: Abashar is nominative as the subject; alternatively, a verb is understood before it.
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r4.anchor: وارتفع «أبشر» على الابتداء. وقيل: بإضمار فعل

QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r5.claim: The plural verb yehdūnanā agrees with bashar as a collective; Arabic can use a singular for a collective noun, as in 12:31.
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r5.anchor: والجمع على معنى بشر ولهذا قال: «يهدوننا» ولم يقل يهدينا.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r6.claim: Arabic may also use a plural in the sense of a singular, as in the verse “What is this, a human?”
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r6.anchor:
وقد يأتي الجمع بمعنى الواحد نحو قوله تعالى:
ما هذا بشرا

QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r7.claim: They disbelieved by saying this dismissively, failing to recognize that God sends whichever servants He chooses.
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r7.anchor: أي بهذا القول إذ قالوه استصغارا ولم يعلموا أن الله يبعث من يشاء إلى عباده

QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r8.claim: Alternatively, they disbelieved the messengers, turned away from the proof, and rejected faith and admonition.
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r8.anchor: وقيل: كفروا بالرسل وتولوا عن البرهان، وأعرضوا عن الإيمان والموعظة.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r9.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r9.claim: Muqātil says God is independent of His servants' obedience through His sovereign power.
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r9.anchor: أي بسلطانه عن طاعة عباده قاله مقاتل.

QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r10.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r10.claim: Another explanation says God's clear proof made Him need no further summons to guide them.
QURTUBI-FULL:64:6/r10.anchor: وقيل: استغنى الله بما أظهره لهم من البرهان وأوضحه لهم من البيان
